key_insight: Erasing phase information while preserving modal amplitudes and same-mode quadratic statistics suppresses the turbulent cascade arrow, but nonlinear Navier–Stokes evolution can rebuild the signed flux.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that controlling or diagnosing turbulence requires more than energy spectra and two-time correlations, because directional energy transfer depends on higher-order phase information and nonlinear dynamics.
method: Build a Haar-distributed Hermitian phase ensemble that keeps prescribed quadratic information intact.
Compare flux statistics under phase-randomized, independent-block, nonlinear-evolution, linear-evolution, and amplitude-matched frozen controls.
Track signed flux and a local cubic geometry scalar to test whether the cascade arrow is recovered.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the phase-Haar ensemble makes the expected odd flux functional zero, strongly suppresses mean transfer and forward-event bias, and that only matched nonlinear Navier–Stokes evolution restores the selected signed-flux scalar near its natural reference.
watch_item: Because high local correlation can persist even after the cascade arrow is erased, local similarity metrics alone may not reliably indicate correct signed energy transfer.
paper_title: Erasing and Regenerating the Turbulent Cascade Arrow
